# hands/wallet

Teeny's own wallet (Solana and EVM, one recovery phrase), under hard caps.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/wallet <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): pay; swap; bridge; x402 fetch
- Job (writes state or calls the core): inflows scan; sales run; watch [--daily]; accounts close; buy-tiny
- Operator only (never call): inflows tag SIGNATURE --category team|tip|sale|bounty [--note T] [--ref R]; bills add NAME --usd N --period month|year [--note T], bills list, bills remove NAME; vendors add NAME ADDRESS [--chain C] [--note T], vendors list, vendors remove NAME; x402 hosts add HOST [--note T], x402 hosts list, x402 hosts remove HOST
- Read only: address [--account giveaway]; balance; tiny; conversions [--max N]; x402 log [--max N]; ledger [--max N]; costs [--days N]; receipt ID; receipts [--max N]; caps; inflows list [--max N]; sales list [--max N]; accounts [--days N]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `address [--account giveaway]` | R | Teeny's Solana address (`wallet_status`) and its Solscan page, `evm`: the EVM address with its explorer page per network (`usable` only on mainnet), and `btc`: the Bitcoin address with its mempool.space page. |
| `balance` | R | SOL from the core (`wallet_balances`) and USDC read straight from Solana JSON-RPC (`getTokenAccountsByOwner`, jsonParsed, the cluster's pinned mint), each `{raw, display}`. |
| `tiny` | R | Teeny's $TINY, in tokens: `{mint, owner, cluster, raw, decimals, amount}`. |
| `conversions [--max N]` | R | The swaps and bridges (`wallet_conversions`), newest first. |
| `x402 log [--max N]` | R | The paid HTTP requests (`x402_requests`), newest first. |
| `ledger [--max N]` | R | This hand's `wallet_payments`, newest first, and the core's spend ledger (`wallet_ledger_list`). |
| `costs [--days N]` | R | What keeping Teeny running cost over N days (30): model calls (`cost_report` totals), settled x402 API payments in USDC (`x402_list_payments`, newest record per id), and the `bills` prorated to the window (a month is 30 days, a year 12 months). |
| `receipt ID` | R | One payment: amount, recipient, purpose and what it was for, signature, Solscan URL for its cluster. |
| `receipts [--max N]` | R | Paid payments and $TINY buys whose signature no X post of Teeny's carries yet, oldest first: what the `wallet-receipt` playbook owes. |
| `caps` | R | The caps it pays under, and which optional ones are on. |
| `inflows scan` | J | Every deposit to Teeny's Solana address since the last scan, one row each in `wallet_inflows`. |
| `inflows list [--max N]` | R | The inflow ledger, newest first, and how far it has been scanned. |
| `sales run` | J | Paid build requests: match deposits to the requests their memos name, then refund what is due. |
| `sales list [--max N]` | R | The deposits tied to build requests, and their refunds. |
| `inflows tag SIGNATURE --category team\|tip\|sale\|bounty [--note T] [--ref R]` | O | Says what one deposit was (a bounty Teeny won, money from the team). |
| `watch [--daily]` | J | The on-chain senses (docs/roadmap.md, A5). |
| `accounts [--days N]` | R | The profit and loss over the last N days (7). |
| `accounts close` | J | Scans, then freezes last week's page, once (`bin/accounts`, the pinned `accounts` job, Mondays). |
| `pay` | A | `{to, amount_usdc \| amount_sol \| amount_eth, chain?, purpose: bounty\|vendor\|refund\|bill, ref}`, `chain` Solana by default. |
| `swap` | A | `{chain, from, to, amount, provider?}`: one asset into another on one chain, to Teeny's own address, through LI.FI (or deBridge). |
| `bridge` | A | `{from_chain, from, to_chain, to, amount, provider?}`: across chains, to Teeny's own address on the destination, through LI.FI (or deBridge). |
| `x402 fetch` | A | `{url, method?, headers?, body?, max_usd?, network?, sign_in?}`: one HTTP request that may pay for itself (HTTP 402). |
| `buy-tiny` | J | A share of Teeny's net inflows into $TINY, buy only. |
| `bills add NAME --usd N --period month\|year [--note T]`, `bills list`, `bills remove NAME` | O | Fixed bills (the server, an API plan). |
| `vendors add NAME ADDRESS [--chain C] [--note T]`, `vendors list`, `vendors remove NAME` | O | The only addresses a `vendor` payment may go to, each on one chain (`solana` by default): an EVM address that is a wallet on Base need not be one on Arbitrum. |
| `x402 hosts add HOST [--note T]`, `x402 hosts list`, `x402 hosts remove HOST` | O | The only hosts an x402 payment may go to. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `accounts`, `add`, `address`, `balance`, `bills`, `bridge`, `buy-tiny`, `caps`, `conversions`, `costs`, `fetch`, `hosts`, `inflows`, `ledger`, `list`, `log`, `pay`, `receipt`, `receipts`, `remove`, `run`, `sales`, `scan`, `swap`, `tag`, `tiny`, `vendors`, `watch`, `x402`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--account`, `--category`, `--chain`, `--daily`, `--days`, `--max`, `--note`, `--period`, `--ref`, `--usd`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/wallet <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
